transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

I’m here because my eating has gotten out of hand, mostly at night. After everyone goes to bed, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers, but then I end up eating a huge amount in one sitting—like half a tray of catered pasta, dessert from a client dinner, and whatever snacks are in the pantry. It feels like more than just being hungry.
Do you feel like you can’t control how much you eat during these nighttime eating episodes, even if you wanted to stop?

Yes. Once I start, especially if it’s been a tense night with my husband, it’s like the part of me that makes decisions just shuts off. I’ll be thinking, “Patricia, stop, that’s enough,” but my hand just keeps going back for more.
Do these nighttime eating episodes cause you significant distress, or have they affected your relationships, work, or daily life in any way?

Yes, it definitely bothers me. I’m still getting my work done, but the mornings after it happens I feel exhausted and really ashamed. And I’ve started skipping things I usually care about, like yoga or time to work on creative stuff, because I just don’t want to face anyone.
After these nighttime eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate for what you’ve eaten?
I don’t really know. I mean, I’m not sure what would count as excessive. I do feel awful afterward, but I don’t have a clear answer beyond that.
After these nighttime eating episodes, have you ever made yourself vomit, used laxatives, or exercised much more than usual to try to make up for what you ate?
I’m still not really sure how to answer that. I know I feel terrible after, but I don’t have a clear memory of doing something like that specifically to make up for it.
After these nighttime eating episodes, have you ever made yourself vomit, used laxatives, or exercised much more than usual to try to make up for what you ate?

I’m sorry, I know you’re asking clearly. I just don’t have a specific memory of doing any of those things to make up for it. I feel bad afterward, but I can’t say that I’ve vomited, used laxatives, or exercised a lot because of it.

Can you describe a typical episode—how long it lasts and whether you feel like you’re eating continuously over a period of time or if it’s more like repeated trips to the kitchen without really stopping to think about it?

It’s usually after everyone’s gone to bed. I’ll think I’m just going to have a little leftovers, but then it turns into more. Like I’ll eat a lot of pasta, then dessert from a dinner, then snacks from the pantry. It feels like it’s all in one sitting, not really a planned meal—more like I keep going and don’t stop to think until I realize how much I’ve had.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you’ve lost control over your eating, like you can’t stop even if you wanted to?

Yes. Once I start, especially if it’s been a tense night with my husband, it feels like the part of me that makes decisions just kind of shuts off. I’ll be thinking, “Patricia, stop, that’s enough,” but I keep reaching for more anyway.
Do these eating episodes only happen at night after you’ve already gone to bed, and are you fully awake and aware of what you’re doing during them?

I’m not totally sure how to separate that. I know it’s usually late, after the house is quiet, but I can’t say it’s only after I’ve actually gone to bed. And yes, I’m awake—I know what I’m doing at the time, even if I feel kind of checked out.
Do these eating episodes happen specifically after you’ve already gone to bed, or are you still up and about when they occur?

I’m not completely sure. A lot of the time I’m still up, like cleaning up or just sitting around after everyone’s gone to bed. I don’t think it’s usually after I’ve already gone to sleep or anything like that.
Have you ever woken up in the middle of the night and felt like you had to eat something before you could go back to sleep?
I don’t really know that I’ve noticed that specifically. If I wake up, I might feel restless, but I can’t say I have to eat before I can fall back asleep.
Have you ever woken up during the night, after trying to fall asleep, and found yourself needing to eat before you could go back to sleep?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve woken up at night before, but I haven’t noticed that I need to eat in order to fall back asleep.
Do you often feel like you’re eating an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time, more than what most people would eat in similar circumstances?

Yes. That’s actually why I came in. After everyone goes to bed, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers, but then it turns into a lot more. Like I’ll realize I’ve eaten half a tray of catered pasta, dessert from a client dinner, and then whatever snacks were in the pantry, all in one sitting. It feels like way more than a normal amount.
Have you ever tried to go to sleep, then woke up later in the night and felt a strong need to eat before you could fall back asleep?
No, I don’t think that’s really happened. I’ve had trouble sleeping sometimes, but I don’t wake up feeling like I have to eat before I can fall back asleep.

Do you have these episodes of eating a large amount of food where you feel like you can’t stop yourself, even if you wanted to, and do you experience these without making up for it later with things like vomiting, fasting, or heavy exercise?

Yes. Once I start, especially after a tense night with my husband, it’s like the decision-making part of me just shuts off. I’ll be thinking, “Patricia, stop, this is enough,” but I still keep reaching for more. And no, I’m not doing things afterward like throwing up or trying to make up for it with extreme exercise or not eating.
